main_issue: Whether the housewarming should serve alcohol (A's purchased drinks) or be alcohol-free because D objects as a Buddhist host.

A-B.evidence: B offered a split-cost refund (18) and a side-table compromise (20), A said it wasn't just money (19); B finally proposed a no-alcohol party (26), which A hadn't accepted by the end.

A-C.evidence: C suggested a cooler box (13) and backed the side-table compromise (21), then offered to repay A for a no-alcohol party (27); A never accepted this and kept insisting on alcohol.

A-D.evidence: A: 'Why are you only bringing this up now' (15), 'We can't have any alcohol at all?' (23); D: 'I can't be one of the hosts if there's alcohol' (24). Neither shifted.

B-C.evidence: They agreed on soft drinks (2-6), C called B's side-table idea a good compromise (21), and C backed B's no-alcohol proposal by offering to pay (27).

B-D.evidence: B first proposed the side-table compromise that D rejected (20, 22), then moved to 'let's just make it a no-alcohol party' (26), which matches D's demand.

C-D.evidence: C proposed the cooler box (13) and endorsed the side-table compromise (21), both rejected by D; then C backed the no-alcohol outcome by offering to repay A (27).
